name: Void Release: Kidan
body:
School evocation [fire, void]; Level psychic 8, shaman 8, sorcerer/wizard 8

Casting Time 1 standard action

Components V, S, DF

Range personal

Effect a number of rays (see text)

Target one or more creatures or objects (see text)

Duration 1 round/level

Saving Throw Reflex half; Spell Resistance yes

Void: Spells with this descriptor are tied with a philosophical school of magic based on a concept known as the Void. The school teaches that the Void is the nothingness from which springs forth creativity, insight, spirit, thought, and also the source of pure energy from which all elements and phenomena are derived. Channeling the power of the Void (or the Void element) allows for the manipulation of the elements in objects and creatures, among other possibilities. Spells with the void descriptor are considered to belong to the Void element (for geomancers) and the void elemental school (for void elementalists).

If a spell has the [void] descriptor, it cannot be dispelled by elements release regardless of how high is your CL.

You unleash rays shaped with the mix of your inner spirit fire and the essence of the Void against your targets. Such rays are known among many martial traditions as ki blasts, energy shots, or simply kidan.

Each ki blast is a ranged touch attack.

You fire two ki blasts initially when you cast this spell.

Thereafter while this spell lasts, you must expend 2 ki points per ki blast you wish to fire. You may fire a ki blast in place of any iterative attacks you make on your turn, using the same BAB as the iterative attacks you are substituting in this way. If a creature provokes an attack of opportunity from you within your natural melee reach, you may fire a ki blast against the provoking creature as your attack of opportunity instead.

A ki blast’s range is long (400 ft. + 40 ft./level) and deals 2d6 points of fire damage and an additional 2d6 points of damage that results directly from the Void (therefore not subject to being reduced by fire resistance).
